Clinical thermometers are used for many.title: Clinical or Laboratory?
Clinical thermometers are used for many.explanation: Clinical thermometers measure body temperature. Laboratory thermometers have many other uses.

options: The bulb
The Celsius scale
The liquid column
The glass tube
Which part is fixed at one end of the th.explanation: The bulb is attached to one end of the thermometer tube.

options: Ice is solid. Liquid water flows. Water vapour spreads.

Water vapour is solid. Ice is liquid. Water changes shape.

Measure water temperature with a laborat.title: Measuring Water Temperature
Measure water temperature with a laborat.body: Use a laboratory thermometer to measure water temperature. Hold it straight up. Do not tilt it. Keep the bulb away from the bottom and sides of the beaker. Keep the bulb in the water while you read it. Wait until the liquid column (the liquid in the tube) stops rising. Then write down the temperature. A room thermometer gives a rough idea of room temperature. Weather reports give the maximum and minimum air temperatures. These values usually change. Air temperature usually rises towards summer. It usually falls in winter.
Measure water temperature with a laborat.explanation: Hold the thermometer straight up. Read it after the liquid column stops rising.
keyPoints: Use a laboratory thermometer the right way to measure water.
Weather reports give the day's maximum and minimum air temperatures.
Air temperature usually rises towards summer. It usually falls in winter.

Use a room thermometer for an approximat.title: Air Temperature Information
Use a room thermometer for an approximat.body: Use a room thermometer for a rough idea of room temperature. Weather reports give the maximum and minimum air temperatures for the day. These readings usually change from day to day. As summer comes, air temperature usually rises. In winter, air temperature usually falls. Read each report carefully. Compare its maximum and minimum values.
Use a room thermometer for an approximat.explanation: Reports tell the highest and lowest air temperatures each day.
keyPoints: A room thermometer gives a rough idea of room temperature.
Weather reports give the day's maximum and minimum air temperatures.
Maximum and minimum temperatures usually change from day to day.

The scientific method starts when you no.title: How scientists solve problems
The scientific method starts when you no.body: Scientists solve problems in steps. First, you notice something. It is interesting or puzzling. This makes you wonder. You think of a question. Then you make the question clear. You guess a possible answer. Next, you test your guess. Use experiments or more observations. This helps people solve problems. It also helps them find new things.
The scientific method starts when you no.explanation: Scientists turn wonder into clear questions and tested guesses.
keyPoints: Noticing something makes us wonder and ask a question.
We make the question clear. We guess a possible answer.
We test the guess with experiments or more observations.

The thermometer shown works from –10 °C.title: Reading the range and divisions
The thermometer shown works from –10 °C.body: The thermometer works from –10 °C to 110 °C. This is its range. Ten small divisions lie between two big marks. Each small division shows 1 °C. To read a temperature, look at the top of the liquid. Find the mark that the top meets.
The thermometer shown works from –10 °C.explanation: Big marks and small divisions help you read the scale.
keyPoints: The range is –10 °C to 110 °C.
Ten small divisions lie between big marks.
Each small division is 1 °C.

Animals differ greatly. They move by fly.title: Animals Move in Different Ways
Animals differ greatly. They move by fly.body: Animals are very different. They move in many ways. Some fly. Some run. Some crawl, walk, hop or jump. They use different body parts to move. Grouping animals helps us understand their variety. Biodiversity means this variety of life. Different animals live in different places. Fish have smooth bodies and fins to swim. Goats live in grassy places and walk on their legs. The Silent Valley movement saved Silent Valley.
Animals differ greatly. They move by fly.explanation: Learning how animals move helps us group them.
keyPoints: Animals move in different ways.
Different body parts help animals move.
Animals live in different places.

A digital thermometer measures temperatu.title: Measuring temperature safely
A digital thermometer measures temperatu.body: A digital thermometer measures temperature by touching your body. Before you use it, wash the tip with soap and water. Then reset it. To measure in the mouth, put it under your tongue. Close your mouth. Wait for a beep or a flashing light. Then take it out. Read the number on the screen. After use, clean the tip with soap and water. Age, time of day and activity can change body temperature.
A digital thermometer measures temperatu.explanation: These steps help you measure body temperature safely.
keyPoints: Wash the tip before and after use.
Reset the thermometer before measuring.
Wait for a beep or flashing light.
Read the temperature on the screen.

Many plant leaves show thin lines. Their.title: Patterns in Leaves, Roots and Seeds
Many plant leaves show thin lines. Their.body: Many plant leaves have thin lines. The pattern of these lines is called venation. A net-like pattern is called reticulate venation. Veins that run side by side are parallel venation. Plants with net-like veins usually have taproots. Plants with parallel veins usually have fibrous roots. Each part of a chickpea seed is a cotyledon. Plants with two cotyledons are dicotyledons. A maize (corn) seed has one thin cotyledon. Plants with seeds like maize are monocotyledons.
Many plant leaves show thin lines. Their.explanation: These patterns help you sort leaves, roots and seeds.
keyPoints: Leaves have net-like or side-by-side veins.
Leaf veins usually match taproots or fibrous roots.
Cotyledons help us name dicotyledons and monocotyledons.

A laboratory thermometer has a long, nar.title: How a laboratory thermometer works
A laboratory thermometer has a long, nar.body: A laboratory thermometer has a long, thin glass tube. The tube is closed. It is the same width all along. A bulb is attached at one end. A thin column of liquid can be seen outside the bulb. The column goes up or down when the temperature changes. Read the temperature where the top of the liquid meets a mark on the Celsius scale. The liquid may be coloured alcohol or mercury.
A laboratory thermometer has a long, nar.explanation: These parts help you read temperature changes.
keyPoints: The tube is long, thin, closed and the same width.
A bulb is attached at one end.
Read where the top of the liquid meets a mark.

Decantation means removing liquid by til.title: Separating tea and other mixtures
Decantation means removing liquid by til.body: Decantation means removing liquid by tilting a container. Sedimentation means a heavy part settles at the bottom. This part does not dissolve in the liquid. Tea leaves settle when the tea is left still. Decanting does not remove every tea leaf. Filtering tea through a strainer separates the leaves. Cloth has very small holes. Filter paper has tiny pores. They trap very small particles. Mud stays behind as residue. The clear liquid that passes through is filtrate.
Decantation means removing liquid by til.explanation: These methods separate the tea leaves from the tea.
keyPoints: Sedimentation makes heavy insoluble parts sink to the bottom.
Decantation removes liquid by tilting a container.
A strainer separates tea leaves from tea.

Living beings show several life characte.title: Signs of Life
Living beings show several life characte.body: Living beings show several signs of life. They grow bigger as they live. They need food. Respiration is the process that includes breathing. Excretion removes waste from the body. A stimulus is something that makes a living being respond. Reproduction makes new living beings of the same kind. Plants also respond. Their flowers open. Touch-me-not leaves fold when touched. A thing with none of these signs is non-living.
Living beings show several life characte.explanation: These signs help you tell living beings from non-living things.
keyPoints: Living beings grow, need food, respire and remove waste.
They respond to stimuli and reproduce.
Plants can move parts but stay in one place.
A thing with no sign of life is non-living.

Science can be studied in outer space an.title: Science Is Everywhere
Science can be studied in outer space an.body: We can study science in outer space and in our kitchens. A playground can also start new discoveries. Many big discoveries came from places no one expected. Science is like a big jigsaw puzzle. It never ends. Each new discovery adds a piece. New knowledge leads to more questions. Then we find more to learn.
Science can be studied in outer space an.explanation: Science is all around us. Each discovery helps us learn more.
keyPoints: We can study science in many places.
Discoveries can start in places no one expects.
Every discovery adds to science.

New discoveries can show that an old ide.title: Discoveries Change Our View
New discoveries can show that an old ide.body: New discoveries can show that an old idea was wrong. They can change how we understand the world. Earth is our home. It is the only planet we know that supports life. We must protect its environment. Earth has many kinds of plants and animals. They live in different regions.
New discoveries can show that an old ide.explanation: New discoveries can change what we understand. They help us protect our home.
keyPoints: Discoveries can correct old ideas.
We must protect Earth's environment.
Plants and animals live in different regions.

Plants and animals can be grouped by the.title: Different Features Make Groups
Plants and animals can be grouped by the.body: We can group plants and animals by similarities and differences. Different groups may use different features. Plants can be grouped by height. They can also be grouped by whether they have flowers. Animals may be grouped by food, place, colour and movement. Grouping helps people study plants and animals more easily.
Plants and animals can be grouped by the.explanation: Different features help us make useful groups.
keyPoints: Groups can use similarities and differences.
Plants may be grouped by height or flowers.
Animals may be grouped by food, place, colour and movement.

A magnet can be identified by the repuls.title: Using a Compass Needle
A magnet can be identified by the repuls.body: You can tell a magnet by repulsion. Repulsion means pushing away. A compass needle is also a magnet. Its North pole moves away from a North pole. It moves closer to a South pole. Wood, cardboard, plastic and glass do not move the needle much. The magnetic effect can pass through non-magnetic materials.
A magnet can be identified by the repuls.explanation: A compass needle helps you see attraction and repulsion.
keyPoints: A compass needle is a magnet.
Repulsion can tell you if something is a magnet.
Magnetic effects pass through non-magnetic materials.

Different countries adopted shared stand.title: Our shared standard units
Different countries adopted shared stand.body: Different countries agreed on shared standard units. This was because travel had caused confusion about measurements. The system we use now is the International System of Units. It is called SI units for short. Its unit of length is the metre. It is written as m. A metre has 100 equal parts. Each part is called a centimetre.
Different countries adopted shared stand.explanation: Shared units help people everywhere measure length clearly.
keyPoints: Shared units reduce confusion when people travel.
The SI unit of length is the metre.
Each part of a metre is called a centimetre.

To test evaporation fairly, change one c.body: To test evaporation fairly, change one thing. Keep everything else the same. For example, compare water in a bottle cap. Compare it with water on a plate. Measure how long each water takes to evaporate completely. The water with a bigger open area should evaporate faster. It needs less time.
To test evaporation fairly, change one c.explanation: Keeping everything else the same helps show the effect.
keyPoints: Change only one thing.
Measure how long the water takes to evaporate completely.
Compare water in a bottle cap and on a plate.

A bar magnet has two poles: the North po.title: Meet the Magnet's Poles
A bar magnet has two poles: the North po.body: A bar magnet has two poles. One is the North pole. The other is the South pole. Iron filings are tiny pieces of iron. Most iron filings stick near the ends of the magnet. Only a few stick to the middle part. If you break a magnet, each piece still has two poles. So, one pole alone cannot exist.
A bar magnet has two poles: the North po.explanation: The ends hold the most iron filings, and every magnet keeps both poles.
keyPoints: The poles are the North pole and the South pole.
Most iron filings stick near the magnet's ends.
Every smaller magnet still has both poles.

Some materials, like glass, water, air a.title: Three kinds of materials
Some materials, like glass, water, air a.body: Glass, water, air and cellophane paper are transparent. You can see clearly through transparent materials. Wood, cardboard and metals are opaque. You cannot see through many opaque materials. Butter paper and frosted glass are translucent. You can see objects through them, but not clearly.
Some materials, like glass, water, air a.explanation: Transparent, opaque and translucent materials help you see in different ways.
keyPoints: Transparent materials let you see clearly.
Opaque materials block your view.
Translucent materials let you see, but not clearly.

Female mosquitoes can spread malaria, de.title: Mosquitoes and Silk Moths
Female mosquitoes can spread malaria, de.body: Female mosquitoes can spread malaria, dengue and chikungunya. So, stop mosquitoes from breeding. Do not let water stay still around you. Mosquito larvae and pupae live in water. They need air. They come up to the surface to breathe. The pupa changes into an adult. The female lays eggs on or near water. Silk moths go through four stages: egg, larva, pupa and adult.
Female mosquitoes can spread malaria, de.explanation: Good learning! These stages and habitats help you understand both life cycles.
keyPoints: Female mosquitoes can spread diseases.
Mosquito larvae and pupae live in water.
Silk moths pass through four stages.

A frog passes through four life stages..title: How a Frog Changes
A frog passes through four life stages..body: A frog goes through four life stages. Its jelly-like eggs are called spawn. Spawn grows into an embryo. A tadpole has a tail but no legs. Later, the tadpole grows hind legs (back legs). A froglet lives in water and on land. The growing frog loses its tail. Its strong legs help it jump. So an adult frog can live in water and on land.
A frog passes through four life stages..explanation: You have followed the main changes in a frog's life.
keyPoints: Spawn are jelly-like frog eggs found in water.
The egg stage grows into the embryo stage.
A frog's habitat changes as it grows.

Air around the Earth is a mixture of sev.title: Air, Breathing and Wind
Air around the Earth is a mixture of sev.body: Air around the Earth is a mixture of gases. It has nitrogen, oxygen, argon, carbon dioxide and other gases. The air we breathe in has oxygen. Our body needs oxygen to do its work. Deep breaths bring more fresh air into your lungs. This helps us stay healthy. Moving air is called wind. Wind makes a firki turn. Windmills can draw water from wells and make electricity.
Air around the Earth is a mixture of sev.explanation: These facts connect breathing, gases, wind and windmill uses.
keyPoints: Air has several gases, including oxygen.
Our body needs oxygen to do its work.
Moving air is called wind.
Wind can help useful machines work.

We often use the scientific method in da.title: Science Is a Shared Journey
We often use the scientific method in da.body: We often use the scientific method in daily life. We all use it a little. Curiosity is the most important quality for learning science. Curiosity means wanting to know things. It helps us ask how and why questions. We should observe (watch carefully) our surroundings. We should explore the many things we do not know. Scientists rarely work alone. So teamwork matters. Science helps us find solutions and solve big problems. It also helps us explore the mysteries of the universe. Science should be a joyful journey.
We often use the scientific method in da.explanation: Curiosity, careful watching and teamwork make science a shared journey.
keyPoints: Use the scientific method in daily life.
Be curious and ask how and why questions.
Observe, explore, solve, and work together.
Enjoy science as a joyful journey.

A nature walk helps you experience the b.title: Many Kinds of Nature
A nature walk helps you experience the b.body: A nature walk helps you see many plants and animals. Watch them, but do not bother them. You can see grass, bushes and big trees. Each bird sings in its own way. Leaves and flowers look different. Frogs can live on land and in water. The variety of life in a place is called biodiversity. Plants and animals need each other.
A nature walk helps you experience the b.explanation: Nature has many differences. We should always be kind to living things.
keyPoints: Watch living things without bothering them.
Leaves and flowers look different.
Plants and animals need each other.

A magnetic compass has a needle-shaped m.body: A magnetic compass has a needle. The needle is a small magnet. It can turn freely. To make one, put an iron sewing needle on a wooden table. Rub it with one pole (end) of a magnet. Do this 30 to 40 times. If pins or iron filings stick, the needle is a magnet. Next, push the needle sideways through a cork. A magnetic compass has a needle-shaped m.explanation: Start with the needle. Magnetise it. Then float it on the cork.
keyPoints: A compass needle can turn freely.
Rubbing it with one pole makes the needle magnetic.
The magnetised needle sits in a cork and floats on water.

Objects can be grouped by properties suc.title: How We Group Materials
Objects can be grouped by properties suc.body: You can group objects by their properties. Properties are things like shape, colour, hardness, softness and shine. Grouping is called classification. One object can use many materials. One material can make many objects. The material we pick depends on its properties and its use. Different parts can use different materials. For example, a pen can have plastic, metal and ink.
Objects can be grouped by properties suc.explanation: These ideas help you group things. They also help you pick useful materials.
keyPoints: Classification means putting objects into groups.
We pick materials by their properties and use.
One object can have different materials.

Tiny water droplets can appear outside a.title: Clues Around Water
Tiny water droplets can appear outside a.body: Tiny drops can appear outside a glass of cold water and ice. The drops may join to make bigger drops. One reason may be that ice melted outside the glass. Condensation means water vapour turns into liquid water. Dew drops appear on plants. Drops gather on the inside of a steel plate over boiling water.
Tiny water droplets can appear outside a.explanation: These clues show that water changes and moves.
keyPoints: Tiny drops can appear outside a cold glass.
Condensation turns water vapour into liquid water.
Drops appear on plants and on a steel plate over boiling water.

Water evaporates at different speeds bec.title: What Affects Evaporation?
Water evaporates at different speeds bec.body: Water evaporates at different speeds. Many things can change this speed. A larger exposed area (open surface) helps water evaporate faster. Sunlight and moving air also make it evaporate faster. Air with more humidity (water in the air) slows evaporation. Rainy days also slow evaporation. A fair test changes only one thing. It keeps the other things the same. It measures how long the water takes to evaporate completely.
Water evaporates at different speeds bec.explanation: These things help you compare evaporation speeds fairly.
keyPoints: Exposed area changes evaporation speed.
Sunlight and moving air speed up evaporation.
Humidity and rainy days slow evaporation.

A germinated seed develops into a seedli.title: How Plants Grow and Move
A germinated seed develops into a seedli.body: A seed that has germinated (started to sprout) grows into a seedling. A seedling has a small root and shoot. In an upright plant, roots grow down and shoots grow up. If you turn a plant upside down, its parts bend. Each part grows in its normal direction. Roots bend down. Shoots bend up. When light comes from one side, the shoot grows towards it. The root keeps growing down.
A germinated seed develops into a seedli.explanation: Plants change how they grow, so they grow correctly.
keyPoints: A seed that germinates becomes a seedling.
Roots grow down and shoots grow up.
Shoots grow towards light from one side.

Rocks break apart over a long time throu.title: How Soil Helps Living Things
Rocks break apart over a long time throu.body: Rocks break into small bits over a long time. The Sun, water and living things break rocks. This is how soil is made. Spaces between soil bits give air and room for roots. Earthworms help turn and loosen soil. Fallen leaves decay (break down) and add nutrients (food) to soil. Soil helps biodiversity. Biodiversity means the variety of living things.
Rocks break apart over a long time throu.explanation: Soil helps many living things. It is very valuable.
keyPoints: Soil forms as rocks break into small bits.
Earthworms and fallen leaves help soil.
Spaces between soil bits give air and room for roots.

On a dark, moonless night, you can see a.title: Our Home Galaxy
On a dark, moonless night, you can see a.body: Look at the sky on a dark night with no moon. You can see a faint (weak) band of light. The band goes from near north to south across the sky. This band is our home galaxy. It is called the Milky Way Galaxy. It is also called Ākāśha Gangā. A galaxy can have millions to billions of stars. Our Solar System is part of it.
On a dark, moonless night, you can see a.explanation: The weak band of light helps us see our home galaxy.
keyPoints: A weak band of light crosses the night sky.
The Milky Way Galaxy is also called Ākāśha Gangā.
Our Solar System is part of the Milky Way Galaxy.

Traditional practices are cooking practi.title: Cooking Then and Now
Traditional practices are cooking practi.body: Traditional practices are old ways of cooking. Modern practices are ways of cooking used today. In the past, most people cooked on a chulha. Today, most people use a modern gas stove. In the past, most grinding was done by hand with a sil-batta. Today, an electric grinder makes grinding easier. Technology, transport and communication have helped cooking practices change.
Traditional practices are cooking practi.explanation: Cooking practices have changed. The reasons and methods are clear.
keyPoints: Traditional and modern cooking practices are different.
Cooking and grinding methods have changed.
Technology, transport and communication helped these changes.

Vitamins and minerals are nutrients that.title: Nutrients that protect you
Vitamins and minerals are nutrients that.body: Vitamins and minerals are nutrients. They help your body work and stay healthy. The chapter lists vitamins A, B1, C and D. It also lists the minerals calcium, iodine and iron. Lemons and oranges give vitamin C. Not having enough vitamin C causes scurvy. Iodised salt is common salt with iodine added. Dietary fibre gives no nutrients. But it helps food move smoothly through your body.
Vitamins and minerals are nutrients that.explanation: Vitamins, minerals and dietary fibre are all important for food and health.
keyPoints: The vitamins listed are A, B1, C and D.
The minerals listed are calcium, iodine and iron.
Dietary fibre helps food move smoothly. It gives no nutrients.

Temperature is a reliable measure of a body's hotness or coldness. A hotter body has a higher temperature than a colder body. The difference between two temperatures shows how their hotness compares. A thermometer measures temperature. Clinical thermometers measure human body temperature. Laboratory thermometers are used for many other purposes. Digital clinical thermometers show temperature on a display and run on batteries. They avoid the risk posed by mercury.

Wait until the liquid column stops rising, then note the temperature. A room thermometer estimates room temperature. Weather reports give maximum and minimum air temperatures. These values usually change, with air temperature generally rising towards summer and falling during winter.

A room thermometer gives a rough idea of room temperature. Weather reports give the maximum and minimum air temperatures. These values usually change. Air temperature usually rises towards summer. The scientific method starts when you notice something interesting or puzzling. Your observation makes you wonder and think of a question. You then make the question clear and guess a possible answer. Next, you test your guess through experiments or further observations. It helps people solve problems and find new things in science and ordinary life.

The thermometer shown works from –10 °C to 110 °C. The temperature difference is found between two bigger marks. Ten small divisions lie between each pair of bigger marks. Each small division represents 1 °C. To read a temperature, find the top of the liquid where it meets a mark.

Animals differ greatly. They move by flying, running, crawling, walking, hopping or jumping, using different body parts. Grouping animals helps us understand their diversity. Biodiversity means this variety of life. Different animals live in different surroundings. Fish have streamlined bodies and fins for movement in water. Goats live in grassy areas and use their legs. The Silent Valley movement saved Silent Valley.

Healthy eating includes wholesome food in moderate quantities. Food is essential in daily life. People in different places eat a variety of foods. Some food items are eaten in many different states, while others are eaten in only one particular state. A state's traditional food is usually based on crops grown there. Soil and climate affect crops. Taste, culture and traditions also affect regional food choices.

Body-based measurements use a person’s body as a unit. A handspan is one such unit, and Deepa’s mother calls it a balisht. People can have different handspan lengths, so the same length may need different numbers of handspans. Every measured length has a number and a unit. A standard unit should give everyone the same measurement for the same length. Scales and measuring tapes are useful because body-based units can differ between people.

A digital thermometer measures temperature when it touches your body. Before use, wash the tip with soap and water, then reset it. For mouth measurement, place it under your tongue and close your mouth. Wait for a beep or a flashing light. Then remove it and read the display. Clean the tip with soap and water after use. Age, time of day and activity level can influence body temperature.

Many plant leaves show thin lines. Their arrangement is called venation. A net-like pattern is reticulate venation. Side-by-side veins show parallel venation. Reticulate plants generally have taproots. Parallel-veined plants generally have fibrous roots. Each part of a chickpea seed is called a cotyledon. Plants with two cotyledons are dicotyledons. A maize seed has one thin cotyledon. Plants with maize-like seeds are monocotyledons.

Many plant leaves have thin lines. The pattern of these lines is called venation. A net-like pattern is called reticulate venation. Veins that run side by side are parallel venation. Plants with net-like veins usually have taproots. Plants with parallel veins usually have fibrous roots. Each part of a chickpea seed is a cotyledon. Plants with two cotyledons are dicotyledons. A maize (corn) seed has one thin cotyledon. Plants with seeds like maize are monocotyledons.

The column goes up or down when the temperature changes. Read the temperature where the top of the liquid meets a mark on the Celsius scale. The liquid may be coloured alcohol or mercury.

Handpicking is removing unwanted pieces from a mixture by hand. It works when particles differ in size, colour and shape. It is convenient when the unwanted particles are few and easy to pick. Malli used his fingers to pick whole black peppers from pulao. To separate grains from stalks, farmers may dry stalks, then beat them on a large wooden log. This beating is called threshing.

Decantation means removing liquid by tilting a vessel. Sedimentation means a heavier part that does not dissolve settles at the bottom. Tea leaves settle because tea is left undisturbed. Decanting does not remove every tea leaf. Filtering tea through a strainer separates the leaves from the tea. Cloth has very small holes. Filter paper has fine pores that trap tiny particles. Mud stays as residue. Clear liquid passing through is filtrate.

Living beings show several life characteristics. They grow larger during their lives and need food. Respiration is the process that includes breathing. Excretion removes waste from the body. A stimulus is an event that makes a living being respond. Reproduction makes new living beings of the same kind. Plants also respond. Their flowers open, and touch-me-not leaves fold when touched. A thing with none of these characteristics is non-living.

Science is like a huge jigsaw puzzle that never ends. Each new discovery adds a piece. New knowledge leads to more questions and more things to find out.

New discoveries can show that an old idea was in the wrong place. They can change how we understand the world. Earth is our home and the only planet we know that supports life. We must protect its environment. Earth has many kinds of plants and animals, and they survive in different regions.

Plants and animals can be grouped by their similarities and differences. Different groups may use different features. Plants may be grouped by height or by the presence or absence of flowers. Animals may be grouped by food, place, colour and movement. Grouping helps people understand and study plants and animals more easily.

A magnet can be identified by the repulsion it produces. A compass needle is also a magnet. Its North pole moves away from a North pole but moves closer to a South pole. Different countries adopted shared standard units because travel had caused confusion about measurements. The system used now is called the International System of Units, or SI units. A stimulus is something that makes a living being respond. Reproduction makes new living beings of the same kind. Plants also respond. Their flowers open. Touch-me-not leaves fold when touched. A thing with none of these signs is non-living.

We can study science in outer space and in our kitchens. A playground can also start new discoveries. Many big discoveries came from places no one expected. Science is like a big jigsaw puzzle. It never ends. Each new discovery adds a piece. New knowledge leads to more questions. Then we find more to learn.

New discoveries can show that an old idea was wrong. They can change how we understand the world. Earth is our home. It is the only planet we know that supports life. We must protect its environment. Earth has many kinds of plants and animals. They live in different regions.

We can group plants and animals by similarities and differences. Different groups may use different features. Plants can be grouped by height. They can also be grouped by whether they have flowers. Animals may be grouped by food, place, colour and movement. Grouping helps people study plants and animals more easily.

You can tell a magnet by repulsion. Repulsion means pushing away. A compass needle is also a magnet. Its North pole moves away from a North pole. It moves closer to a South pole. Wood, cardboard, plastic and glass do not move the needle much. The magnetic effect can pass through non-magnetic materials.

Different countries agreed on shared standard units. This was because travel had caused confusion about measurements. The system we use now is the International System of Units. It is called SI units for short. Its unit of length is the metre. It is written as m. A metre has 100 equal parts. Each part is called a centimetre.

To test evaporation fairly, change one condition and keep every other condition the same. For example, compare water in a bottle cap with water spread on a plate. The investigation measures the time needed for each water sample to evaporate completely. The sample with a larger exposed area should evaporate faster. It should need less time.

A bar magnet has two poles: the North pole and the South pole. Iron filings are tiny pieces of iron. The greatest number stick near the magnet's ends. Only a few stick to the remaining part. If you break a magnet, each smaller piece still has a North pole and a South pole. So, one pole alone cannot exist.

Some materials, like glass, water, air and cellophane paper, are transparent. You can see clearly through transparent materials. Other materials, like wood, cardboard and metals, are opaque. You cannot see at all through many opaque materials. Materials like butter paper and frosted glass are translucent. You can see objects through them, but not clearly.

A clinical thermometer cannot measure boiling water or ice. Celsius, Fahrenheit, and Kelvin use °C, °F, and K. Celsius is degree Celsius, and Fahrenheit is degree Fahrenheit. Kelvin is kelvin and the SI unit of temperature. The three scales were named after the scientists who developed them. To convert Celsius to Kelvin, add 273.15. Leave a space between a temperature number and its unit. Use degrees above one degree.

Female mosquitoes can spread malaria, dengue and chikungunya, so mosquito breeding should be prevented. Do not let water stagnate around you. Mosquito larvae and pupae live in water and need air. They come to the surface to breathe. The pupa changes into an adult, and the female lays eggs on or near water. Silk moths pass through egg, larva, pupa and adult stages.

A frog passes through four life stages. Its jelly-like eggs, called spawn, develop into an embryo. A tadpole has a tail but no legs. Later, the tadpole gains hind legs. A froglet lives in water and on land. The growing frog loses its tail. Its strong legs help it jump, so an adult frog can live in water and on land.

Air around the Earth is a mixture of several gases. It contains nitrogen, oxygen, argon, carbon dioxide and other gases. The air we breathe in contains oxygen. Our body needs oxygen to carry out its activities. Taking deep breaths brings more fresh air into the lungs and helps us stay healthy. Moving air is called wind. Wind makes a firki rotate. Windmills can draw water from wells and generate electricity.

We often use the scientific method in daily life. We all use it to some extent. Curiosity is the first and foremost quality for learning science. It helps us ask how and why questions. We should observe our surroundings carefully and explore the many unknown things. Scientific work is rarely done alone, so teamwork matters. Science helps us find solutions, solve bigger problems, and explore universe mysteries. Science should be a joyful journey of exploration.

They come up to the surface to breathe. The pupa changes into an adult. The female lays eggs on or near water. Silk moths go through four stages: egg, larva, pupa and adult.

A froglet lives in water and on land. The growing frog loses its tail. Its strong legs help it jump. So an adult frog can live in water and on land.

Deep breaths bring more fresh air into your lungs. This helps us stay healthy. Moving air is called wind. Wind makes a firki turn. Windmills can draw water from wells and make electricity.

We often use the scientific method in daily life. We all use it a little. Curiosity is the most important quality for learning science. Curiosity means wanting to know things. It helps us ask how and why questions. We should observe (watch carefully) our surroundings. We should explore the many things we do not know. Scientists rarely work alone. So teamwork matters. Science helps us find solutions and solve big problems. It also helps us explore the mysteries of the universe. Science should be a joyful journey.

A nature walk helps you experience the beauty and variety of plants and animals. You should respect living creatures and observe them without disturbing them. Grasses, bushes and large trees are part of the walk. Birds each have unique chirps. Leaves and flowers differ in many ways. Frogs can live on land and in water. A region's variety of plants and animals is called biodiversity. Plants and animals depend on one another.

A magnetic compass has a needle-shaped magnet that can rotate freely. This means the needle can turn easily. To make one, place an iron sewing needle on a wooden table. Stroke it with one pole of a magnet 30 to 40 times. If pins or iron filings stick to it, the needle has become a magnet. Next, pass the magnetised needle horizontally through a cork and float both in water.

Objects can be grouped by properties such as shape, colour, hardness, softness and shine. This is called classification. One object may use different materials, while one material may make many objects. Material choice depends on its properties and the object's purpose. Different parts may use different materials. A pen, for example, may contain plastic, metal and ink.

Tiny water droplets can appear outside a glass tumbler holding cold water and ice. The droplets may combine to make bigger drops. One possible reason is that ice melted outside the tumbler. Condensation means water vapour changing into liquid water. Dew drops appear on plants. Water drops gather on the inner side of a steel plate covering boiling water.

Water evaporates at different speeds because several conditions can affect it. A larger exposed area helps water evaporate faster. Sunlight and more movement of air also make it evaporate faster. Air with more humidity and rainy days slow evaporation. A fair investigation changes one condition while keeping the others the same. It measures the time needed for the water to evaporate completely.

A germinated seed develops into a seedling with a small root and shoot. In an upright plant, the root grows downwards and the shoot grows upwards. If the plant is turned upside down, each part bends and grows in its usual direction. The root bends downwards, while the shoot bends upwards. When light comes from one direction, the shoot grows towards it. The root keeps growing downwards.

Rocks break apart over a long time through the Sun, water and living organisms. This is how soil forms. Spaces between soil particles give air and room for roots. Earthworms help turn and loosen soil. Fallen leaves decay, meaning they break down and add nutrients. Soil supports biodiversity, which means the variety of living things.

On a dark, moonless night, you can see a faint band of light across the sky. The band stretches from near north to south. This band is our home galaxy, the Milky Way Galaxy, also called Ākāśha Gangā. A galaxy can contain millions to billions of stars. Our Solar System is part of it.

A nature walk helps you see many plants and animals. Watch them, but do not bother them. You can see grass, bushes and big trees. Each bird sings in its own way. Leaves and flowers look different. Frogs can live on land and in water. The variety of life in a place is called biodiversity. Plants and animals need each other.

A magnetic compass has a needle. The needle is a small magnet. It can turn freely. To make one, put an iron sewing needle on a wooden table. Rub it with one pole (end) of a magnet. Do this 30 to 40 times. If pins or iron filings stick, the needle is a magnet. Next, push the needle sideways through a cork. Float the cork and needle in water.

You can group objects by their properties. Properties are things like shape, colour, hardness, softness and shine. Grouping is called classification. One object can use many materials. One material can make many objects. The material we pick depends on its properties and its use. Different parts can use different materials. For example, a pen can have plastic, metal and ink.

Tiny drops can appear outside a glass of cold water and ice. The drops may join to make bigger drops. One reason may be that ice melted outside the glass. Condensation means water vapour turns into liquid water. Dew drops appear on plants. Drops gather on the inside of a steel plate over boiling water.

Water evaporates at different speeds. Many things can change this speed. A larger exposed area (open surface) helps water evaporate faster. Sunlight and moving air also make it evaporate faster. Air with more humidity (water in the air) slows evaporation. Rainy days also slow evaporation. A fair test changes only one thing. It keeps the other things the same. It measures how long the water takes to evaporate completely.

A seed that has germinated (started to sprout) grows into a seedling. A seedling has a small root and shoot. In an upright plant, roots grow down and shoots grow up. If you turn a plant upside down, its parts bend. Each part grows in its normal direction. Roots bend down. Shoots bend up. When light comes from one side, the shoot grows towards it. The root keeps growing down.

Rocks break into small bits over a long time. The Sun, water and living things break rocks. This is how soil is made. Spaces between soil bits give air and room for roots. Earthworms help turn and loosen soil. Fallen leaves decay (break down) and add nutrients (food) to soil. Soil helps biodiversity. Biodiversity means the variety of living things.

Look at the sky on a dark night with no moon. You can see a faint (weak) band of light. The band goes from near north to south across the sky. This band is our home galaxy. It is called the Milky Way Galaxy. It is also called Ākāśha Gangā. A galaxy can have millions to billions of stars. Our Solar System is part of it.

Traditional practices are cooking practices from earlier times. Modern practices are cooking practices used today. Earlier, most cooking was done on a chulha. Today, most people use a modern gas stove. Earlier, most grinding was done by hand with a sil-batta. Today, an electrical grinder makes grinding easier. Technology, transport and communication have helped cooking practices change.

Vitamins and minerals are nutrients that help your body work and stay healthy. The chapter lists vitamins A, B1, C and D, plus minerals calcium, iodine and iron. Lemons and oranges provide vitamin C, while a lack of vitamin C causes scurvy. Iodised salt is common salt with the required amount of iodine salts added. Dietary fibre gives no nutrients, but helps food move smoothly through your body.

Vitamins and minerals are protective nutrients because they help your body function and stay healthy. The chapter lists vitamins A, B1, C and D, and minerals calcium, iodine and iron. Some nutrients can be lost when food is cooked at high heat. Dietary fibre provides no nutrients, but helps food move smoothly through the body.

A balanced diet contains essential nutrients, roughage and water. It gives these in the right amounts. Your needs can change with age, gender, physical activity and health. Millets contribute significantly to a balanced diet. Junk foods are high in sugar and fat, but low in useful nutrients. Eating them frequently can make a person obese.

Food miles show how far food travels from its producer to the consumer. Reducing food miles can support local farmers. It can also keep food fresh and healthy. Fortified foods have nutrients added during food processing. This improves their nutritional quality. Iodised salt and some baby foods are examples of fortified foods. The FSSAI regulates food quality in India.

Like poles repel each other, so two North poles push apart. Two South poles also push apart. Unlike poles attract each other, so a North pole pulls towards a South pole. Both ends of an iron bar are attracted by a magnet. A compass needle is also a magnet, so it can show these pushes and pulls.

Distance can look different when people measure from different houses. Their observations can agree if they measure from the same object or point. This fixed starting point is called a reference point. Padma used Delhi as her reference point. The stones showed 70 km and then 60 km. Padma was getting closer to Delhi.

Linear motion means moving along a straight line. Circular motion means moving along a circular path. Oscillatory motion means moving to and fro about a fixed position. Periodic motion repeats a path after a fixed interval of time. A fixed interval means the same time gap each time. Both circular and oscillatory motion are periodic.

Traditional practices are old ways of cooking. Modern practices are ways of cooking used today. In the past, most people cooked on a chulha. Today, most people use a modern gas stove. In the past, most grinding was done by hand with a sil-batta. Today, an electric grinder makes grinding easier. Technology, transport and communication have helped cooking practices change.

Vitamins and minerals are nutrients. They help your body work and stay healthy. The chapter lists vitamins A, B1, C and D. It also lists the minerals calcium, iodine and iron. Lemons and oranges give vitamin C. Not having enough vitamin C causes scurvy. Iodised salt is common salt with iodine added. Dietary fibre gives no nutrients. But it helps food move smoothly through your body.

Vitamins and minerals are protective nutrients. They help your body work and stay healthy. The chapter lists vitamins A, B1, C and D. It also lists the minerals calcium, iodine and iron. Some nutrients can be lost when food is cooked at high heat. Dietary fibre gives no nutrients. But it helps food move smoothly through the body.

A balanced diet has nutrients, roughage and water. It has them in the right amounts. Your needs can change with age, gender, activity and health. Millets are very helpful for a balanced diet. Junk food has a lot of sugar and fat. It has few useful nutrients. Eating junk food often can make a person obese.

Food miles show how far food travels. It goes from the producer to the consumer. The producer grows or makes the food. The consumer buys and eats it. Cutting food miles can help local farmers. It can also keep food fresh and healthy. Fortified foods have nutrients added when they are made. This makes their nutrition better. Iodised salt and some baby foods are examples of fortified foods. The FSSAI makes rules for food quality in India.

Like poles repel each other. Repel means push away. Two North poles push apart. Two South poles push apart too. Unlike poles attract each other. Attract means pull together. A North pole pulls towards a South pole. A magnet attracts both ends of an iron bar. A compass needle is also a magnet. So it can show these pushes and pulls.

Distance can look different when people measure from different houses. Their results can match if they measure from the same object or point. A starting point that does not move is a reference point. Padma used Delhi as her reference point. The stones on the road showed 70 km, then 60 km. Padma was getting closer to Delhi.

Linear motion means moving along a straight line. Circular motion means moving around in a circle. Oscillatory motion means moving back and forth around one place. Periodic motion repeats its path after a fixed interval of time. A fixed interval means the same time gap every time. Both circular and oscillatory motion are periodic.

Appearance tells us what a material looks like. Freshly cut, unpolished wood has a distinct appearance. Lustrous means shiny, while non-lustrous means not shiny. Shiny surfaces usually look lustrous, but not every shiny material is a metal. Hard materials resist compression and scratches. Soft materials are easily compressed or scratched. Hardness and softness are relative, so we compare materials.

Mass tells whether an object is heavier or lighter. More mass means heavier, and less mass means lighter. Volume is the space occupied by water. Two tumblers can have the same capacity but hold different amounts of water. Water bottles show volume in litres or millilitres, written L and mL. Mass uses the kilogram, written kg. The cubic metre is the volume unit. One cubic metre equals 1000 litres.

Some bodies are hotter than other bodies. Tap water may feel hotter than cold water from a matka. Touch cannot always tell us how hot or cold something is. An investigation uses warm water in A. B has tap water. C has ice-cold water. Hands placed in different water can make the same tap water feel different. Touch cannot always decide whether a body is hot or cold.

The states of water behave differently. Ice keeps its own shape in any container. Liquid water flows and changes its shape, but its volume stays the same. Water vapour spreads throughout the available space. Heating moves water from ice to liquid water, and then to water vapour.

Water moves between the Earth's surface and the atmosphere. This movement is called the water cycle. Water vapour is water in the air that can form clouds around tiny dust particles. Burnt newspaper provides tiny dust particles. Small droplets float in the air and form clouds. Moist sand has water in it. Water drops that become heavy fall as rain. Under special conditions, water may fall as hail or snow.

Most water on Earth is in oceans and seas, where it is salty. Freshwater appears as ice, snow, rivers, lakes and underground water. Only a small part is easily accessible. Polluted water cannot be consumed. Turning off taps and repairing leaks reduces wastage. Rainwater harvesting stores rain for later use.

Plants can be grouped by their seed parts. Each part of a chickpea seed is called a cotyledon. Plants with two cotyledons are called dicotyledons. A maize seed has one thin cotyledon. Plants with maize-like seeds are called monocotyledons. Dicots generally have reticulate venation and taproot systems. Parallel-veined plants generally have fibrous roots.

Plants and animals live in a habitat. A habitat provides food, water, air, shelter and other needs for survival. Special features that help them survive in a region are adaptations. Deserts have very little water. Desert plants can store water in thick stems. Deodar trees have a cone-like shape and sloping branches.

Appearance means how a material looks. Freshly cut wood that is not polished has its own look. Lustrous means shiny. Non-lustrous means not shiny. Shiny surfaces are usually lustrous. But not every shiny thing is a metal. Hard materials are not easily squashed or scratched. Soft materials are easily squashed or scratched. We must compare materials to say hard or soft.

Water has three states. They behave in different ways. Ice keeps its own shape in any container. Liquid water flows and takes the shape of its container. Its volume stays the same. Water vapour spreads out to fill all the space. Heating changes ice into liquid water. More heating changes liquid water into vapour.

Most water on Earth is in oceans and seas. This water is salty. Fresh water is in ice, snow, rivers, lakes, and under the ground. Only a small part is easy to use. Polluted water is dirty. We cannot drink it. Turning off taps and fixing leaks saves water. Rainwater harvesting means saving rain for later.

Plants can be grouped by their seed parts. Each part of a chickpea seed is called a cotyledon. Plants with two cotyledons are called dicotyledons. A maize seed has one thin cotyledon. Plants with maize-like seeds are called monocotyledons. Dicots usually have reticulate venation and taproot systems. Parallel-veined plants usually have fibrous roots.

Plants and animals live in a habitat. A habitat gives food, water, air and shelter. Special features that help them survive are called adaptations. Deserts have very little water. Desert plants can store water in thick stems. Deodar trees have a cone-like shape and sloping branches.

Land habitats are places where plants and animals live on land. Aquatic habitats are water places, such as ponds, lakes, rivers and oceans. Frogs can live in water and on land. Animals that can live in both are called amphibians. Protecting habitats protects homes, food and biodiversity.

Carbohydrates, fats and proteins are food components. Common sugar is a carbohydrate. Many oils belong to fats. Nuts provide fat, and fat stores energy for the body. Milk products and pulses provide protein. People get protein from plants and animals. Protein helps the body grow and repair itself.

Travellers used a magnetic compass to find directions when stars could not be seen. Lodestones are natural magnets, discovered long ago. People later learned that magnets can be made from iron. Magnets in pencil boxes, stickers and toys are artificial magnets. Magnets can have many different shapes. Objects attracted to a magnet stick to it. These materials are called magnetic materials. Iron is a magnetic material.

Choose a scale that suits the length. A pencil fits a 15-cm scale. A room's height may need a metre scale. Use flexible tape for a tree's girth. Place the scale beside the object and touch it along its length. Keep your eye above the tip. If zero is unclear, use another full mark. A measurement needs a number and its unit. For curved lines, use flexible tape or thread.

Motion depends on the reference point you choose. A reference point helps us decide whether something is at rest or in motion. Use the bus as the reference point. The passengers stayed in their seats, so they were at rest. Use a building outside as the reference point. Then both the passengers and the bus were moving.

Water can be seen in three states in daily life. In the solid state, water is ice. Heating melts ice into liquid water. Further heating changes water into gaseous water vapour. Ice keeps its shape, liquid water flows, and water vapour spreads throughout available space.

A bean plant starts as a seed. With suitable conditions, it germinates and grows into a young plant. Germination means beginning to grow. It develops leaves, flowers, fruit and eventually dies. Its flowers can dry, while remaining flower parts can become a pod. This pod holds seeds, which can grow into new bean plants. This whole journey is the plant's life cycle.

The larva and pupa are different mosquito stages. Both live in water and need air for respiration. They come to the water surface to get air. Kerosene oil forms a thin layer over the water’s surface. The pupa later changes into an adult mosquito. An adult female lays eggs on or near water, continuing the cycle.

The Sun is Earth's main energy source. Its heat and light help us and living things. Sunlight helps plants prepare food, and grass needs it to grow. Animals get energy by eating plants. Solar panels capture sunlight and produce electricity. Forests contain many plants and shelter wild animals, birds and insects. Cutting trees reduces forest cover, and restoring a forest takes many years.

Natural resources come from nature. People also make human-made resources to meet their needs. Renewable resources are restored within a reasonable time. Air, water and forests are renewable natural resources. Minerals, soil, rocks, coal, petroleum and natural gas are non-renewable resources. We must conserve natural resources and use them responsibly for the future.

Asteroids are small rocky objects. Many travel around the Sun between Mars and Jupiter. This region is called the asteroid belt. Comets are objects with long tails. They are made of dust, gases, rocks and ice. Frozen material in a comet starts evaporating when it nears the Sun. A comet becomes dim as it moves away from the Sun. Scientists understand comets as icy-rocky visitors travelling near the Sun.

We often find answers without noticing it. A stopped pen gives us a problem to investigate. First, ask why it has stopped writing. One possible answer is that the ink has finished. Open the pen to check. An empty refill tells us that our guess was correct. If not, try another answer. The ink might have dried up, so test the new guess.

Water can be a solid, a liquid or a gas. Ice is solid water. Heat melts ice into liquid water. More heat changes water into a gas. This gas is called water vapour. Ice keeps its shape. Liquid water flows. Water vapour spreads out to fill any space.

Then the plant dies. Its flowers can dry up. Other flower parts can become a pod. A pod holds seeds. These seeds can grow into new bean plants. This whole journey is the plant's life cycle.
